judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: This is the 'TikTok for Business' link in the Google ad banner iframe Home_0. The other two links with this name are the 'TIKTOK FOR BUSINESS' links in the tower ads Home_4 and Home_5, which show the same TikTok creative. I decoded the adurl parameter of each href in the snapshot. All three lead to the same landing page, https://ads.tiktok.com/business/pt-BR/industries/cpg, with the same campaign parameters. The hrefs differ only in Google click-tracking tokens (ai, sig, cid, gclid), so 'lead to 3 different places' is wrong. The link text names the advertiser and describes the purpose on its own. Identical text with an equivalent purpose does not fail 2.4.4, and even the AAA identical-name rules would pass it. Rampa had the hrefs, adurl included, and treated tracking redirects as different destinations.

judgments.label: uncertain
judgments.rationale: This is the 'Abrir' CTA in the Home_0 ad banner, in an iframe labelled 'Publicidade'. The claim that nothing around it tells where it goes is doubtful. In the snapshot it shares a row container (readingText 'TikTok for Business Abrir') with the adjacent 'TikTok for Business' link, which goes to the same landing page. The rest of the ad ('Cadastre-se no TikTok', the description) is in the same small ad document, and the screenshot shows 'TikTok for Business ... Abrir >' on one line. But the context sits in generic divs, not in a paragraph, list item, table cell, aria-describedby or aria-labelledby. That is not one of the relationships the 2.4.4 Understanding document and techniques H77/H78/H79/G53/ARIA7/ARIA8 name. Strict auditors would fail the generic 'Abrir'; others would accept the self-contained ad card as its context. Competent auditors would disagree, so it is not a clear true positive.
